What "no artificial sweeteners" actually means

Artificial sweeteners are the non-nutritive, synthetic sweeteners brand makers reach for when they want zero-sugar sweetness without giving up flavor. This guide screens every bar for four of them: sucralose, acesulfame potassium, aspartame, and saccharin.

20.4% of the 1181 bars in our database still have one on the label. Here is how often each one shows up, and where it usually hides.

Sucralose
241 bars20.4%
Usually shows up as a flavor-rounding sweetener in low-sugar or high-fiber bars, often alongside allulose or fiber syrups to hit a specific sugar number on the label.
Found in: 1st Phorm, Addra Labs, Anabar, Atkins
and 25 moreHide, BSN, BalanceDiet, Barebells, David, Einstein, Equate, FITCRUNCH, Fulfil, GNC Total Lean, Genius Gourmet, JiMMYBAR!, Legendary, MRE BAR, MTN OPS, Musashi, MyProtein, Neoh, NuGo, One, Power Crunch, Pure Protein, Quest, SOAR, Wonderslim, think!
Acesulfame Potassium
18 bars1.5%
Almost always paired with sucralose rather than used on its own, adding a sweetness boost on top of the primary sweetener.
Found in: BalanceDiet, David
Aspartame
0 bars0.0%
Not currently used in any bar we track. Once common in diet foods generally, it has largely fallen out of favor in the protein bar category.
Found in: No bars in the current database
Saccharin
0 bars0.0%
Not currently used in any bar we track. The oldest artificial sweetener on this screen, now rare in this category.
Found in: No bars in the current database

What we found screening 1181 bars

20.4%
of bars contain an artificial sweetener
241 of 1181 bars contain sucralose, acesulfame potassium, aspartame, or saccharin. Sucralose alone accounts for nearly all of it, showing up across low-sugar and high-fiber bars at every price point.
43.6% of sucralose bars list it as a real ingredient, not a trace amount.
Only 105 of 241 bars containing sucralose list it inside a "contains 2% or less" clause. The rest, including Anabar Monster Cookie Crunch, Anabar Fluff n' Butter, name it directly among the main ingredients.
Quest disqualifies completely.
All 16 tracked Quest flavors contain sucralose, part of how the brand hits its low-sugar, high-fiber macro targets across the entire lineup.
Barebells disqualifies completely too.
25 of 25 Barebells flavors contain sucralose, the same sweetener behind most of the disqualified bars on this list.
Whole-food bars dominate the qualifying pool.
KIND, Larabar, Bobo's, Aloha, and GoMacro all qualify at or near 100%. Their sweetness comes from dates, fruit, or honey rather than a manufactured sweetener.
A mixed lineup is common, not rare.
NuGo, Wonderslim, think!, and 1st Phorm are examples of brands that split meaningfully between qualifying and disqualified flavors within the same lineup.
148 brands still represented.
Even with 20.4% of the database disqualified, the qualifying pool spans a wide range of protein levels, price points, and ingredient grades.
Acesulfame potassium never shows up alone.
All 18 bars containing acesulfame potassium also contain sucralose. Neither David nor BalanceDiet, the only two brands using it, use it as a standalone sweetener.

Frequently asked questions

We screen for Sucralose, Acesulfame Potassium, Aspartame, and Saccharin. These are the non-nutritive artificial sweeteners that actually show up in protein bar ingredient lists. Any bar listing one of these gets flagged, regardless of how small the amount looks on the label.
No. Stevia leaf extract, Reb A, and monk fruit (luo han guo) extract are plant-derived sweeteners, not synthetic ones, so they don't count against a bar on this page. They show up constantly in the qualifying bars on this list. If you want to avoid all non-sugar sweeteners, including plant-derived ones, check the ingredient list yourself.
Yes, by a wide margin. Sucralose shows up in 241 of the 1181 bars we track, about 20%. Acesulfame potassium is a distant second, and we found zero bars in the current database containing aspartame or saccharin.
Yes, across the entire lineup. All 16 tracked Quest flavors contain sucralose, part of how the brand hits its low-sugar, high-fiber numbers.
Yes. All 25 Barebells flavors contain sucralose, the same sweetener driving most of the artificial-sweetener bars on this list.
940 bars across 148 brands clear our artificial sweetener screen, led by whole-food brands like KIND, Larabar, and Bobo's that qualify at or near 100%. The full ranked list is in the table below, sorted by ingredient quality.
Not especially. It shows up in 18 of the 1181 bars we track, mostly concentrated in just two brands, David and BalanceDiet, almost always stacked alongside sucralose rather than used alone.
Yes, and it's common. NuGo splits mostly clean: 28 of 30 flavors qualify. Wonderslim and think! split the other way, with the majority of their lineups landing on the disqualified side.
Sucralose and acesulfame potassium add intense sweetness with zero sugar and negligible calories, which is why they show up so often in bars marketed as "low sugar," "keto friendly," or high-protein with a low calorie count. The tradeoff for some people is an artificial aftertaste or a personal preference to avoid non-nutritive sweeteners altogether.
